08A2974E.description: Heavy chest-supported horizontal pull — builds the lat and mid-back strength that drives paddle power.
techniqueCues: Chest on the pad, neutral spine, squeeze shoulder blades before each pull
Row to lower chest — elbows drive back along your sides
Pause and squeeze lats at the top, think paddle catch
Control the negative; don't bounce the weight
08A2974E.injuryNotes: Keep hips pinned to the pad — lifting off reduces back engagement and risks strain.

A2D838BD.description: High-to-low cable rotation — mirrors the torso twist of cutbacks and off-the-lip snaps.
techniqueCues: Pulley at shoulder height, stand sideways with a wide base
Pull diagonally down across your body — hips stay square
Brace your core and rotate through the thoracic spine
Control the return; don't let the cable whip you back
A2D838BD.injuryNotes: Start light — excessive lumbar rotation under load can irritate the lower back.

D7D7FCCE.description: Heavy horizontal pull that builds paddle-power back strength with a stable hip hinge.
techniqueCues: Hinge at the hips, neutral spine, elbows drive back
Squeeze shoulder blades at the top
Row to upper stomach — think paddle catch
Control the eccentric; don't rest the bar on the floor
D7D7FCCE.injuryNotes: Keep the lower back flat — if it rounds, reduce load.

983274DD.description: Full-body power move linking leg drive to overhead press — pop-up and paddle posture in one.
techniqueCues: Squat deep, drive through heels
Press the bar up and slightly forward as you stand
Brace hard at the top
Lower under control to chest, then squat
983274DD.injuryNotes: Avoid overarching the lower back at lockout.

914F3A96.description: Chest-supported row for pure pulling strength without lower-back fatigue — great paddle-volume work.
techniqueCues: Chest flat on incline bench, arms hang straight
Row dumbbells high, elbows past your torso
Squeeze lats and mid-back at the top
Slow negative — no swinging
914F3A96.injuryNotes: Keep neck neutral; don't crane to look forward.

018ADC12.description: Explosive barbell row from a dead stop — builds the fast pull strength behind a powerful paddle stroke.
techniqueCues: Torso parallel to floor, bar rests on ground each rep
Explode the bar to lower chest
Elbows drive back, not out
Reset fully between reps
018ADC12.injuryNotes: Requires solid hip hinge — scale with dumbbell rows if lower back is sensitive.

C732C341.description: Single-arm landmine row with a long lever — targets lats and grip for extended paddle sessions.
techniqueCues: Staggered stance, elbow tracks close to your side
Pull to hip pocket, pause at peak contraction
Keep hips square — resist rotation
Full stretch at the bottom without dumping the shoulder
C732C341.injuryNotes: Use straps only when grip is the limiter, not as a default.

05487216.description: Alternating kettlebell rows in a hinged position — paddle-style pulling with anti-rotation core demand.
techniqueCues: Wide stance, hips back, flat back
Row one bell while the other anchors you
Fight the twist — stay square
Alternate smoothly, no jerking
05487216.injuryNotes: Keep hamstrings loaded; don't squat the weight up.

67280085.description: Lat and serratus expansion under load — opens the paddle arc and overhead reach.
techniqueCues: Lie on bench, slight bend in elbows throughout
Lower the dumbbell behind your head with control
Feel the stretch across lats and rib cage
Pull back over chest in an arc, not a press
67280085.injuryNotes: Use moderate weight — shoulder impingement risk if elbows flare or weight is too heavy.

F51D9080.description: Explosive full-body slam — trains the violent hip extension and rotation of turns.
techniqueCues: Lift the ball overhead, brace your core
Slam straight down by hinging and rotating slightly
Catch on the bounce or pick up cleanly
Every rep should be maximal intent
F51D9080.injuryNotes: Use a non-bouncing ball on hard floors; watch foot placement.

108D7A14.description: Eccentric hamstring strength for pop-up drive and knee stability in deep carves.
techniqueCues: Knees anchored, hips high, body straight
Lower as slowly as possible
Use hands to push back up only as needed
Keep hips extended throughout the descent
108D7A14.injuryNotes: Very demanding — start with short ranges and band assistance.

487B3755.description: Unilateral hip extension for single-leg pop-up power and stance stability.
techniqueCues: Upper back on bench, one foot planted
Drive through the heel to full hip extension
Squeeze glute at the top, ribs down
Control the descent — no collapsing
487B3755.injuryNotes: Keep the pelvis level — don't rotate open at the top.

E8D86EE8.description: Rear delt and scapular activation — keeps shoulders healthy through high paddle volume.
techniqueCues: Arms straight, pull the band apart to chest height
Squeeze shoulder blades, externally rotate slightly
Hold briefly at end range
Slow return — stay tall
E8D86EE8.injuryNotes: Use a light band; this is prehab, not max effort.

BB792A36.description: Full-body conditioning that mimics the pop-up-to-stance transition under fatigue.
techniqueCues: Chest to floor, hips snap up
Feet land ready to move — soft and athletic
Stand tall at the top before the next rep
Breathe rhythmically; don't rush form
BB792A36.injuryNotes: Modify to step-back burpees if wrists or low back are irritated.

BD0AD077.description: Contralateral core stability — trains the cross-body connection used in paddling and rotation.
techniqueCues: On all fours, extend opposite arm and leg
Keep hips level — no rocking
Reach long through fingertips and heel
Hold 2–3 seconds, switch sides
BD0AD077.injuryNotes: Reduce range if lower back arches excessively.

F3717B0E.description: Explosive hip drive and overhead catch — builds the fast power for pop-ups and late drops.
techniqueCues: Hinge, bell between legs
Explode hips, pull elbow high
Punch overhead in one motion
Absorb the landing softly
F3717B0E.injuryNotes: Master the one-arm swing before adding the snatch.

FA5D0DE1.description: Triple extension power pull — trains violent hip and pull sequencing for explosive surfing.
techniqueCues: Hinge, neutral spine, bar close
Drive hips forward, shrug, then pull high
Elbows lead above the bar
Lower under control
FA5D0DE1.injuryNotes: Not a row — keep it explosive but don't muscle with the arms alone.

2A48E443.description: Hamstring and glute hinge with straight legs — builds posterior chain length and strength for deep surf stance.
techniqueCues: Feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot
Hinge at the hips, legs stay straight with soft knees
Bar travels in a straight vertical line close to the body
Squeeze glutes at the top, slow eccentric stretch
2A48E443.injuryNotes: Keep the back flat — if it rounds, reduce range or load.

B923B230.description: Trap-bar deadlift with neutral grip — posterior chain power with less lower-back stress than conventional.
techniqueCues: Stand inside the bar, grip handles, chest up
Push the floor away, hips and knees extend together
Lock out with glutes, not hyperextension
Hinge back on the descent, bar stays vertical
B923B230.injuryNotes: Great alternative if conventional deadlift bothers your lower back.

72CFFAD5.description: Hip-hinge with dumbbells — hamstring and glute strength for pop-up drive and single-leg stability.
techniqueCues: Soft knees, hinge until you feel hamstring tension
Dumbbells trace down the front of your legs
Drive hips forward to stand, squeeze glutes
Keep ribs down — no lower-back arch at the top
72CFFAD5.injuryNotes: Start light; ROM beats weight for surf transfer.

40C6A9FC.description: Front-loaded squat with the bar in your elbows — builds upright leg strength and core bracing for a stable surf stance.
techniqueCues: Bar rests in the crease of your elbows, pressed against your stomach
Stay tall through the chest, brace your abs hard
Sit between your heels, knees track over toes
Drive through the heels to stand, exhale at the top
40C6A9FC.injuryNotes: Pad your elbows or use a thick bar sleeve if the bar digs in — build load gradually.

BA3DE542.description: Barbell jump with an explosive shrug — trains triple-extension power for pop-ups and fast turns.
techniqueCues: Overhand grip just outside the thighs, slight hip hinge
Dip the knees, then drive through the floor like a vertical jump
Shrug shoulders to your ears at the top — bar stays close
Land soft and reset; this is power, not a max shrug
BA3DE542.injuryNotes: Keep load moderate; avoid bouncing reps if your traps or lower back feel tight.

4F5866F8.description: Low-back emphasis on the 45° bench — erector endurance for upright paddle posture.
techniqueCues: Pad support over the hips — hip crease at the top edge of the pad
Rise straight in one line — minimal hip hinge, torso stays rigid
Arms crossed or plate held tight to the chest
Stop at neutral; don't over-arch at the top
4F5866F8.injuryNotes: If you feel sharp lumbar pain, lower the pad or switch to the glute setup.

091737FA.description: Loaded low-back hyperextension — builds erector strength for long paddle sessions.
techniqueCues: Pad over the hips, same straight-torso setup as bodyweight low-back version
Hold the plate tight to your chest — load stays close to the body
Rise in a straight line; squeeze erectors, not glutes
Lower with control — no bouncing at the bottom
091737FA.injuryNotes: Start light; this targets the lower back directly under load.

6A6C31A5.description: Wide-grip cable lat pulldown — builds the vertical pull strength behind paddle power.
techniqueCues: Thighs pinned under the pad, slight lean back, shoulders down
Pull the bar to upper chest — elbows drive down and slightly back
Squeeze lats at the bottom; think paddle catch
Control the return; don't let the stack yank your shoulders up
6A6C31A5.injuryNotes: Avoid behind-the-neck pulldowns — pull to the front of the chest only.

867AC3B6.description: Feet-up (Larsen) bench press — strict chest press with legs off the floor, removing leg drive for pure pressing strength.
techniqueCues: Lie on the bench with legs extended — feet off the floor (flying feet)
Shoulder blades pinned, slight arch, bar to mid-chest
Press without using leg drive or hip bridge
Control the descent — this exposes weak points in your chest press
867AC3B6.injuryNotes: Use less weight than your regular bench; the strict setup loads the shoulders and chest differently.

F72FA239.description: Dumbbell squeeze press — constant inward pressure on the bells for inner-chest and triceps work.
techniqueCues: Lie back with dumbbells squeezed together over your chest, neutral grip
Keep pressing the bells into each other throughout the rep
Lower to mid-chest, then press up and slightly inward
Shoulders pinned — don't let elbows flare wide
F72FA239.injuryNotes: Use moderate weight; the squeeze fatigues wrists and forearms faster than a normal press.

651F844C.description: High-pulley cable crossover — upper chest and anterior delt squeeze from a standing fly.
techniqueCues: Pulleys set high, step forward into a stable staggered stance
Slight bend in elbows, arms sweep down and in toward your hips
Squeeze chest hard at the bottom — knuckles meet in front
Control the stretch on the way back; don't let cables pull your shoulders forward
651F844C.injuryNotes: Start light — the long lever at high pulleys stresses the shoulder capsule if you rush the stretch.

C315DC2A.description: High-pulley cable crossover for shoulders — rear delt and upper-back focus, paired with the chest crossover.
techniqueCues: Pulleys set high, cross handles in front at shoulder height
Arms stay mostly straight — pull back and out, not down to the hips
Squeeze rear delts and mid-back at the end range
Control the return; don't let the stack wrench your shoulders forward
C315DC2A.injuryNotes: Keep weight light — this is isolation work for shoulder health and posture, not max loading.

DE68C825.description: Single-arm cable lateral raise from a low pulley — targets the side delt for shoulder width and paddle stability.
techniqueCues: Low pulley, stand sideways — free hand on the frame for balance
Slight bend in the working elbow, cable crosses in front of your body at the start
Raise your arm out to the side until wrist and elbow are at shoulder height
Lower with control; switch sides after each set
DE68C825.injuryNotes: Don't shrug the trap or swing — if you need momentum, the weight is too heavy.

2DBCA395.description: Bayesian (behind-the-back) cable curl — elbows behind the torso for a deep bicep stretch and long-head emphasis.
techniqueCues: Low pulley behind you, handles in hand, step forward so arms trail behind your hips
Staggered stance, chest up, elbows fixed behind your torso
Curl without letting elbows drift forward — squeeze at the top
Lower slowly for a full stretch behind the body
2DBCA395.injuryNotes: Start light — the stretched position loads the bicep tendon; avoid swinging or heaving the weight.

234897AB.description: Neutral-grip cable hammer curl with a rope — brachialis and forearm strength for paddle grip and board carry.
techniqueCues: Low pulley with rope, neutral grip (palms facing each other)
Elbows pinned to your sides, shoulders back
Curl the rope to chest height without swinging
Lower with control — full extension at the bottom
234897AB.injuryNotes: Keep wrists neutral; don't let elbows drift forward on the curl.
